svg.title: Why the triangles wait
svg.desc: Two tilted ellipses meet the same origin-centered circle of radius 321. The earlier ellipse has two intersections and the later ellipse has four. A radial close-up shows a flat shoulder appearing at phase 0.89494082717179 pi. Before and at that threshold every positive fold count has at most two visits to a point. Four ellipse points at one radius do not assert four visits to one spatial point. Circle counts are exact; the paths and marked positions are numerical illustrations.
svg.text: ALDEBARAN · THE ELLIPSE INSIDE THE TURN
A third visit needs a third ellipse point at the same radius.
A shoulder makes room for two more points
Radius along one piece of the ellipse. The rest lies outside this close-up.
At the threshold: a flat shoulder
The radial obstruction ends at 0.894940827171…π, for every positive fold count.
